paper: KISS-ICP: In Defense of Point-to-Point ICP (RA-L 2023)
recorded_with: reproduce.py: official kiss-icp 1.3.0, KITTI dataloader, 141-frame KITTI 00 sub-sequence rebuilt from the benchmark Zenodo release; plus stage 2 (downstream localizability) via work/registration_utility.py + work/export_normalized_maps.py
note: This is NOT the paper's number and the checks do not compare against it. KISS-ICP's metric is the KITTI devkit one with 100-800 m segments; this trajectory is 108.3 m, so it yields exactly 2 samples against the paper's hundreds over full sequences. The value is tracked so drift in the code path is caught, not as a reproduction claim. Reproducing 0.50 % needs KITTI odometry registration.

metrics.regutil_headline: L2: AA ranking dufomap > beautymap > removert_port > removert_official > uncleaned > erasor_port; registration-failure ranking removert_port < dufomap < removert_official < beautymap < uncleaned < erasor_port

environment.patch_required: pipeline.py:130 float() on a shape-(1,) array - NumPy 2 removed it; see work/local_patches.patch
environment.data_gap: KITTI/MulRan/Boreas registration-gated; Newer College download broken upstream

stage2.question: task book §6 H1' - does the map-quality ranking agree with the ranking by whether a robot can still register into the cleaned map?
stage2.protocol: every map normalised to 0.2 m, then Open3D point-to-plane ICP of each of the 141 frames from a deliberately wrong initial guess; success = <0.2 m, <2 deg, inlier ratio >= 0.30
stage2.limitation: self-registration (the maps were built from these frames), so absolute rates are optimistic and only the ranking comparison is claimed
stage2.excluded: erasor_official - different coordinate frame (official SuMa/bag frame)
